nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Soil microbial community restoration_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the primary purpose of the study described in the abstract?
nodes.answer: The primary purpose was to investigate how different organic and inorganic fertilization regimes affect the temporal stability of microbial communities in the rhizosphere of sorghum at various growth stages.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Soil microbial community restoration_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What findings were reported regarding the stability of microbial communities in organic manure treatments?
nodes.answer: The findings indicated that microbial co-occurrence networks in organic manure treatments were more robust, suggesting greater stability of microbial community temporal variation in organically fertilized soils.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Soil microbial community restoration_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why is understanding microbial community stability important?
nodes.answer: Understanding microbial community stability is important because it contributes to the prediction of shifts in ecosystem functions in response to climate change and agricultural management practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Soil microbial community restoration_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What concept describes a microbial community's higher ability to resist and recover from disturbances?
nodes.answer: The concept that describes this ability is known as microbiome stability.
